clue.text: Pirate and girl embrace love on a ship

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the next pieces inside it, as arms embrace someone

parts.note: Barbara is a girl's name

indicators.note: the love letter sits on, that is just before, the ship's letters

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A buccaneer and his sweetheart kiss aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' puts OSS inside BARBARA, between its R and final A. Barbarossa was the name given to notorious Barbary corsairs of the 16th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarossa ('Redbeard') was the nickname of the Ottoman corsair Hayreddin and his brother, famed sea raiders.

indicators.note: a name lying buried inside the snowslide word is concealed within its letters

explanation.surface: Some poor man has been lost under a snowslide.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so a fair stand-in for an unnamed male person.

clue.text: Important person gives an extensive lecture

parts.note: extensive means big, large in scope
to wig someone is an old British verb meaning to rebuke or lecture them

explanation.surface: A VIP delivers a long talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wig' as a verb, to scold, is old British slang and unfamiliar to many solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is informal for a person of high rank or influence.

clue.text: Explorer with a girl he seduced

indicators.note: seduced suggests these letters are led astray from their proper order

explanation.surface: An adventurer took a young woman along and won her over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seduced' rearranges A GIRL HE. Sir Walter Raleigh was the Elizabethan courtier who sailed to the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh led expeditions to Guiana and the New World, making him a famous Elizabethan voyager.

explanation.surface: A sports club takes advantage of a spinning ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is one of the opposing sides in a match; in snooker and billiards, side is the spin put on the cue ball.

parts.note: high-flown usually means pompous prose, but here it is letters literally flown high in an aeroplane

explanation.surface: Pretentious literary works.
explanation.definitionFit: Post carried by aircraft is letters that travel at altitude, so writings that have flown high.

clue.text: About to be beaten but don't turn back

explanation.surface: Someone on the verge of losing, urged not to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To face defeat is both to be on the brink of losing and, read literally, to confront loss head-on rather than flee.

clue.text: Bachelor of Education student ragged about being untidy

parts.note: BEd is the abbreviation for the teaching degree Bachelor of Education

indicators.note: the word ragged goes around the student letter, surrounding it

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee teacher's scruffy appearance gets him mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside, giving RAGGLED. 'Ragged' looks like a verb meaning teased, but it is just its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled describes someone dishevelled and messy, as after rain or rough handling.

explanation.surface: A friend invited round for a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a friend or partner; maté is a South American herbal infusion drunk like tea.

parts.note: powerless suggests a weak fan, but it means an engineless craft holding up a pilot in a recent airborne pastime

explanation.surface: A feeble fan of a newfangled game.
explanation.definitionFit: The unpowered kite-like wing carries, or supports, its flier in a sport that began in the 1960s and 70s.

indicators.note: origins says the clue word is only the raw material, to be reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A falling star comes from somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' signals that the letters of REMOTE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a fragment of space rock burning up in the atmosphere, popularly called a falling star.

clue.text: Saucy girl the guard will keep his eye on?

definitions.text: the guard will keep his eye on?

explanation.surface: A cheeky young woman is watched by a railway guard.
explanation.walkthrough: A train guard keeps watch over the luggage in the van.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage is dated slang for a pert or impudent young woman, and also luggage, which a railway guard looks after.

clue.text: Delivery is not left, though one is entitled to it

parts.note: delivery of a baby is its birth
the side that is not left is the right

explanation.surface: A newborn arriving on the right-hand side has an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is a privilege or inheritance due to someone by virtue of descent.

parts.note: a textile mill worker beginning the shift would literally begin making cloth on a loom

explanation.surface: Clock on at the textile factory.
explanation.definitionFit: To get weaving is British informal for to get busy or start working hard; read literally it is beginning to make cloth.

indicators.note: to be signals that the word agree turns into, or becomes, another arrangement

explanation.surface: Consenting to show enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms meaning enthusiastic or impatient to act.

clue.text: There's a tonic in eggs scrambled around mid-morning

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece, holding it inside
scrambled eggs are mixed up, so these letters are jumbled
mid picks out the centre letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A breakfast of scrambled eggs at half-past ten contains a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' gives GINSEG; 'around' puts the middle letter of the seven-letter MORNING inside it, before the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a root taken as a restorative remedy, believed to boost energy.

explanation.surface: Foolish creatures who nonetheless rescued a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the sacred geese on Rome's Capitol cackled and woke the defenders against a Gallic night attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a fool, and the birds of Juno's temple saved the Roman Capitol, a pun on capital.

explanation.surface: A woman paired with a male swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a woman's name; a cob, or cobnut, is the nut of a variety of hazel tree.

parts.note: food that goes off will rot

explanation.surface: Leave, taking a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a roster of turns or duties.

explanation.surface: Number up and narrate again.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell is to count (as votes in a teller's tally) and to relate a story.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
comfort means ease, relief from discomfort

explanation.surface: Quit offering chilly consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cease is a synonym for halt or end.

clue.text: Garment paid for on receipt in Massachusetts

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
COD is cash on delivery, payment made when goods are received

explanation.surface: A cloak bought cash on delivery from somewhere in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is the hook-shaped peninsula on the coast of the US state.

clue.text: Ten fuddled with drink weave around

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled by drink, so these letters are confused

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Ten people befuddled with booze stagger around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuddled' gives the anagram ENT; 'weave around' looks like a drunk's walk but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or interlace things together.

clue.text: Lean over the counter where your shoes are repaired

parts.note: a ship that leans over is said to heel
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Someone leans across the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel bar is a British shop or kiosk doing quick shoe repairs and key cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's booth for fast shoe mending, usually in a station or shopping centre.

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, giving these letters a new shape

explanation.surface: A proper change has been implemented.
explanation.definitionFit: Enacted means put into effect or performed, as a law or a plan.

clue.text: Number start to clean out and scrub

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, and it is told to start, coming first

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the word clean is jumbled

explanation.surface: A housekeeper is told to begin cleaning out and scouring.
explanation.walkthrough: C (a hundred) starts things off; 'out' turns CLEAN into ANCEL. 'Scrub' looks like part of the cleaning picture but means call off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for calling it off.

clue.text: Ask one to join the party?

definitions.text: Ask one to join the party?

parts.words: Ask one to join the party?
parts.note: sounds like political recruitment, but means requesting someone come to a social gathering

explanation.surface: Recruit a member for a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite is to request someone's company at an event such as a celebration.

clue.text: Burden of love to rising star

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: Lovers bear a heavy load as a star ascends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SUN into NUS beneath O.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation one must bear.

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a banknote is a bill in American usage

explanation.surface: Tuition fees at a private school are increasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns NOTE into the school's name. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the elite English public school near Windsor.

indicators.note: outrageous means wild, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Café prices are scandalous, so get a takeaway instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges COST IN CAFE. 'Take-away' suggests a carry-out meal but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to seize property officially, removing it from its owner.

explanation.surface: A small measure of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a unit of four inches used for horses' height, and a cluster of bananas.

clue.text: Deadly sin spreading around N American place of entertainment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the single letter, enclosing it
spreading suggests the letters fan out into a new arrangement

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for North in North American

explanation.surface: Sin is spreading across North American amusement venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' turns DEADLY SIN into DISEYLAND; 'around' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is the theme park in Anaheim, California, a resort of rides and shows.
